People Are In Awe Of How 'Dancing With The Stars' Contestant Ezra Frech Expertly Handled His Prosthetic Leg Falling Off Mid-Performance

"The way Alan clocked it, grabbed the prosthetic, and waited so respectfully until Ezra or Dani were ready to grab it - I lost it 😭"

Stephanie Soteriou— BuzzFeed

LOADINGERROR LOADING

On Tuesday, Paralympian Ezra Frech, 21, made Dancing with the Stars history as he became both the first amputee and the youngest male winner of the show, alongside his professional partner Daniella Karagach.

Eric McCandless / Getty Images

Advertisement

If you didn’t know, Ezra was born with congenital limb differences. For him, this meant that he was born without most of his left leg, including his knee and fibula, which is the calf bone. He was also missing all but one finger on his left hand.

Rich Polk / Getty Images

At age 8, Ezra fell in love with sports, and he made his Paralympics debut at the 2020 Tokyo games when he was just 16 years old. At the 2024 Summer Paralympics in Paris, he won two gold medals: one for the Men’s 100m, and the other for the Men’s High Jump.

Fernando Leon / Getty Images

And during last night’s DWTS finale, viewers were left seriously impressed by the expert way that Ezra handled his prosthetic leg coming off during his and Daniella’s final dance.

In case you missed it, Ezra and Daniella were performing a freestyle routine to Linkin Park’s song “Numb,” with the performance paying tribute to people with disabilities. Ezra started the routine with his prosthetic leg off, but around 35 seconds in, he went behind a screen to attach it.

However, it fell off just seconds later, after Ezra performed a jump, forcing him to continue with the routine with just one leg — including lifting Daniella.

Professional dancer Alan Bersten quickly picked the prosthetic up from the dance floor and held onto it until Ezra was able to find the time to put it back on partway through the routine:

Judge Derek Hough acknowledged how swiftly Ezra recovered from the potentially devastating moment, telling him: “The worst-case scenario might have happened and you wouldn’t even have known, the way you rose to that moment.”

Those watching at home were equally impressed, with content creator Kenzie Greene Burroughs’s Instagram reel about the moment going viral. On it, she wrote: “genuinely SO impressed by how quickly ezra recovered when his prosthetic fell off!!! he just kept dancing.”

Ser Baffo / Getty Images

Somebody else commented on the post: “Holy crap, I didn’t even realize he actually did lift her on one leg. I was so focused on the fact that he was standing that I failed to miss he actually lifted her.” One more added: “He deserved that win before this dance but this moment was so incredibly powerful. He didn’t let it define the dance.”

Somebody else wrote: “As a wheelchair user I was sobbing uncontrollably. Words can’t describe what it means to see this on the biggest stage, fully accepted and imperfect and beautiful.” Another observed: “The way Alan clocked it, grabbed the prosthetic, and waited so respectfully until Ezra or Dani were ready to grab it - I lost it 😭.”

Somebody else concluded: “Honestly it made the whole thing better bc it showed how much harder it was for him and how he still thrived.”

Speaking to ExtraTV after he was crowned the winner of the show, Ezra said of his leg: “I knew it wasn’t on right. I haven’t watched the video back, but you can see I’m fidgeting with it as I was running up; it wasn’t on right. Sometimes it’ll lock into place, even if it’s not on right, so I had to just go, and then when I jumped, I was like, ‘Oh my God, it’s gonna come off!’ And then it came off; everything happened so fast. I was prepared to dance the rest of the freestyle on one leg if I had to, and then [Daniella] yelled: ‘Put on your leg!’ And I heard that, immediately... I don’t even know what happened; I blacked out. Everything happened so fast.”

Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach on #DWTS Season 35 win and the moment his prosthetic leg fell off during the freestyle. 🪩 pic.twitter.com/HVcRo7l0na

In their victory, Ezra and Daniella beat Olympic figure skater Amber Glenn and her professional partner Pasha Pashkov, who came second, and comedian and internet personality Connor Wood and his professional partner Rylee Arnold, who took third place.
